quote: The TSA is governed by Delaware law with exclusive jurisdiction in Delaware state courts... APA § 10.12 (Order of Precedence) provides that the APA controls over Ancillary Agreements in case of conflict, "except that each Ancillary Agreement controls as to its specific subject matter." One could argue that governing law is the TSA's "specific subject matter," in which case Delaware law applies to TSA disputes. But if a claim arises that implicates both the APA and the TSA... the parties could end up litigating in two forums under two bodies of law... Recommended fix. Conform TSA § 9.3 to the other documents: ...Laws of the State of New York... courts located in New York County, New York
reason: Issue 3 meets every element of the criterion. It identifies TSA § 9.3 as choosing Delaware law and Delaware courts, against the APA's New York law and New York County forum. It explains that APA § 10.12 lets the TSA control its own subject matter, so the Delaware choice is not overridden. It flags the risk of related disputes being split across two forums under two bodies of law. It recommends redrafting TSA § 9.3 to New York law and New York County courts.
